42426.title: Wilson disease

definition.value: Wilson disease is a disorder of copper metabolism that, when untreated, can present with hepatic, neurologic, or psychiatric disturbances – or a combination of these – in individuals ages three years to older than 70 years. Manifestations in untreated individuals vary among and within families. Liver disease can include recurrent jaundice, simple acute self-limited hepatitis-like illness, autoimmune-type hepatitis, fulminant hepatic failure, or chronic liver disease. Neurologic presentations can include dysarthria, movement disorders (tremors, involuntary movements, chorea, choreoathetosis), dystonia (mask-like facies, rigidity, gait disturbance, pseudobulbar involvement), dysautonomia, seizures, sleep disorders, or insomnia. Psychiatric disturbances can include depression, bipolar disorder / bipolar spectrum disorder, neurotic behaviors, personality changes, or psychosis. Other multisystem involvement can include the eye (Kayser-Fleischer rings), hemolytic anemia, the kidneys, the endocrine glands, and the heart.

Symptom</SemanticType><Definition>Continuous involuntary sustained muscle contraction. When an affected muscle is passively stretched, the degree of resistance remains constant regardless of the rate at which the muscle is stretched. This feature helps to distinguish rigidity from muscle spasticity.</Definition></ClinicalFeature><ClinicalFeature uid="45244" CUI="C0029408" TUI="T047" SDUI="HP:0002758"><Name>Osteoarthritis</Name><SemanticType>Disease or Syndrome</SemanticType><Definition>Osteoarthritis (OA) is a degenerative disease of the joints characterized by degradation of the hyaline articular cartilage and remodeling of the subchondral bone with sclerosis (Meulenbelt et al., 2006). Clinical problems include pain and joint stiffness often leading to significant disability and joint replacement. Osteoarthritis exhibits a clear predilection for specific joints; it appears most commonly in the hip and knee joints and lumbar and cervical spine, as well as in the distal interphalangeal and the first carpometacarpal (base of thumb) and proximal interphalangeal joints of the hand; however, patients with osteoarthritis may have 1, a few, or all of these sites affected (Stefansson et al., 2003). According to a conservative estimate, greater than 70% of the population of the United States at age 65 years is affected by the disease, reflecting its age dependence. Genetic Heterogeneity of Susceptibility to Osteoarthritis Susceptibility to osteoarthritis has been associated with variation in other genes: OS2 (140600) with variation in the MATN3 gene (602109) on chromosome 2p24; OS3 (607850) with variation in the ASPN gene (608135) on chromosome 9q22; and OS5 (612400) with variation in the GDF5 gene (601146) on chromosome 20q11. Other susceptibility loci for osteoarthritis have been mapped to chromosomes 2q33 (OS4; 610839) and 3p24 (OS6; 612401).</Definition></ClinicalFeature><ClinicalFeature uid="14533" CUI="C0029442" TUI="T047" SDUI="HP:0002749"><Name>Osteomalacia</Name><SemanticType>Disease or Syndrome</SemanticType><Definition>Osteomalacia is a general term for bone weakness owing to a defect in mineralization of the protein framework known as osteoid. This defective mineralization is mainly caused by lack in vitamin D. Osteomalacia in children is known as rickets.</Definition></ClinicalFeature><ClinicalFeature uid="14535" CUI="C0029456" TUI="T047" SDUI="HP:0000939"><Name>Osteoporosis</Name><SemanticType>Disease or Syndrome</SemanticType><Definition>Osteoporotic fractures are an important public health problem affecting both sexes. The pathogenesis of osteoporosis is complex and involves both environmental and genetic components. Osteoporotic bone is characterized by decreased bone strength, reflected by a decreased bone mineral density (BMD) and disrupted microarchitecture. Bone is remodeled continuously during adult life, and osteoporosis is typically the result of an imbalance in bone remodeling, with resorption exceeding formation (summary by Tofteng et al., 2007). See BMND1 (601884) for a list of bone mineral density (BMD) quantitative trait loci, some of which have been associated with susceptibility to osteoporosis. Association has been suggested between variation in the ESR1 gene (133430) and BMD.</Definition></ClinicalFeature><ClinicalFeature uid="10976" CUI="C0033687" TUI="T033" SDUI="HP:0000093"><Name>Proteinuria</Name><SemanticType>Finding</SemanticType><Definition>Increased levels of protein in the urine.</Definition></ClinicalFeature><ClinicalFeature uid="20693" CUI="C0036572" TUI="T184" SDUI="HP:0001250"><Name>Seizure</Name><SemanticType>Sign or Symptom</SemanticType><Definition>A seizure is an intermittent abnormality of nervous system physiology characterized by a transient occurrence of signs and/or symptoms due to abnormal excessive or synchronous neuronal activity in the brain.</Definition></ClinicalFeature><ClinicalFeature uid="52469" CUI="C0038002" TUI="T033" SDUI="HP:0001744"><Name>Splenomegaly</Name><SemanticType>Finding</SemanticType><Definition>Abnormal increased size of the spleen.</Definition></ClinicalFeature><ClinicalFeature uid="52737" CUI="C0040034" TUI="T047" SDUI="HP:0001873"><Name>Thrombocytopenia</Name><SemanticType>Disease or Syndrome</SemanticType><Definition>A reduction in the number of circulating thrombocytes.</Definition></ClinicalFeature><ClinicalFeature uid="21635" CUI="C0040822" TUI="T184" SDUI="HP:0001337"><Name>Tremor</Name><SemanticType>Sign or Symptom</SemanticType><Definition>An unintentional, oscillating to-and-fro muscle movement about a joint axis.</Definition></ClinicalFeature><ClinicalFeature uid="12124" CUI="C0042963" TUI="T184" SDUI="HP:0002013"><Name>Vomiting</Name><SemanticType>Sign or Symptom</SemanticType><Definition>Forceful ejection of the contents of the stomach through the mouth by means of a series of involuntary spasmic contractions.</Definition></ClinicalFeature><ClinicalFeature uid="88444" CUI="C0085605" TUI="T047" SDUI="HP:0001399"><Name>Liver failure</Name><SemanticType>Disease or Syndrome</SemanticType><Definition>A disorder characterized by the inability of the liver to metabolize chemicals in the body. Causes include cirrhosis and drug-induced hepatotoxicity. Signs and symptoms include jaundice and encephalopathy. Laboratory test results reveal abnormal plasma levels of ammonia, bilirubin, lactic dehydrogenase, and alkaline phosphatase.</Definition></ClinicalFeature><ClinicalFeature uid="39223" CUI="C0086439" TUI="T033" SDUI="HP:0002375"><Name>Hypokinesia</Name><SemanticType>Finding</SemanticType><Definition>Abnormally diminished motor activity. In contrast to paralysis, hypokinesia is not characterized by a lack of motor strength, but rather by a poverty of movement. The typical habitual movements (e.g., folding the arms, crossing the legs) are reduced in frequency.</Definition></ClinicalFeature><ClinicalFeature uid="57484" CUI="C0151747" TUI="T047" SDUI="HP:0000124"><Name>Renal tubular dysfunction</Name><SemanticType>Disease or Syndrome</SemanticType><Definition>Abnormal function of the renal tubule. The basic functional unit of the kidney, the nephron, consists of a renal corpuscle attached to a renal tubule, with roughly 0.8 to 1.5 nephrons per adult kidney. The functions of the renal tubule include reabsorption of water, electrolytes, glucose, and amino acids and secretion of substances such as uric acid.</Definition></ClinicalFeature><ClinicalFeature uid="57497" CUI="C0151904" TUI="T033" SDUI="HP:0031956"><Name>Elevated circulating aspartate aminotransferase concentration</Name><SemanticType>Finding</SemanticType><Definition>The concentration of aspartate aminotransferase (AST) in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.</Definition></ClinicalFeature><ClinicalFeature uid="57740" CUI="C0151905" TUI="T033" SDUI="HP:0031964"><Name>Elevated circulating alanine aminotransferase concentration</Name><SemanticType>Finding</SemanticType><Definition>An abnormally high concentration in the circulation of alanine aminotransferase (ALT).</Definition></ClinicalFeature><ClinicalFeature uid="57502" CUI="C0152025" TUI="T047" SDUI="HP:0001271"><Name>Polyneuropathy</Name><SemanticType>Disease or Syndrome</SemanticType><Definition>A generalized disorder of peripheral nerves.</Definition></ClinicalFeature><ClinicalFeature uid="57539" CUI="C0152457" TUI="T047" SDUI="HP:0200032"><Name>Kayser-Fleischer ring</Name><SemanticType>Disease or Syndrome</SemanticType><Definition>Grey-green or brownish-pigmented ring in the deep epithelial layers at the outer border of the cornea.</Definition></ClinicalFeature><ClinicalFeature uid="58125" CUI="C0162557" TUI="T047" SDUI="HP:0006554"><Name>Acute liver failure</Name><SemanticType>Disease or Syndrome</SemanticType><Definition>Hepatic failure refers to the inability of the liver to perform its normal synthetic and metabolic functions, which can result in coagulopathy and alteration in the mental status of a previously healthy individual.
